record_notes.DCP-LETT-1610F: December 4 with 1854 supplied from sale catalogue, possibly a postmark, not a directly observed postmark. Complete two-page ALS, three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Provisional present to be kept tidy and returned if needed; sharing restricted to two separately identified Sarah Elizabeth Wedgwoods (sister-in-law and aunt), not one person. Possible advance Sydney Smith memoir only editorial conjecture; later 1855 reading log does not prove completed reading December 4. Conditional custody not permanent gift or already enacted lending.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1390: February 17, supplied 1851, complete ALS. Two blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. To William Jackson Hooker, forwards Joseph Dalton Hooker letter for eventual return; knowledge of tropical oaks/birches and Falconer obstruction identifies November 26, 1850 source1371 alongside explicit apparatus. Does not answer Joseph here. Joseph homecoming and workload prospective; March25 actual arrival later. Father receipt and return of enclosure unproved. New cross-correspondent witness records knowledge by February17 without exact receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1428F: May 25, supplied 1851, complete four-page ALS; F suffix is not fragment. Three blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Thanks Horner family for sympathy on Annie and answers missing inquiry after Emma; mother and newborn essentially well but strength/spirits recovering slowly. Horner continental trip and Lyell Cape/India voyage hoped, not completed. P2 reports Emma requested affectionate love in Charles prose, not separate surviving Emma letter. Missing Horner condolence cannot be replaced by Susan or Catherine similar subject.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1709: July 2, 1855 Hunt ALS. Eight blocks, five footnotes, Darwin annotations and bibliography. Explicitly answers missing Darwin May7 letter forwarded from St Michaels; no exact receipt. Bat species judgment based on appearance, promised deputy inquiry and specimen still future. Quail island movements hearsay not personal observation; summer mountain movement and muteness questioned. Coastal seed measurements from memory, Acacia identity tentative, dispatch and domestic-breed information promised. Later June1,1856 Darwin-to-Hooker seed forwarding is a follow-up probe, not proof July1855 receipt. Citation to own1844/45 article and permission to cite name do not establish Darwin already read it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1479: April16, supplied1852 from mourning paper comparison, ALS. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Balanus larvae received by writing, previously seen form, fine specimens expected to become useful and promised preservation. No demonstrated novel discovery, completed later use or surviving incoming cover. Later1854 discussion does not specifically identify these specimens.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13870: Incomplete note attributed to Innes by handwriting/content, after February8 through August1855 from captaincy and Hore address; source exact date and authorship remain qualified. Five blocks, ten footnotes and separate Darwin annotations. Hore address and no Ainslie water communication are separate opening matters. Pointer bitch appeared pure, one setter personally remembered; repeated litters hearsay, either Tournay or Johnson ownership uncertain. Suggested witnesses not independently corroborating statements. General crossing/reappearance observation distinct from Darwin later pencil qualification about ultimate absorption, which is undated. No missing preceding inquiry reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1452: September7,1851 autograph copy by Jeffreys (ACCS), not simply unqualified delivered ALS. Ten blocks, ten footnotes and bibliography. Answers missing August31 Darwin inquiry received on return home, exact receipt unstated. Notes may be retained, specimens to be returned when done; label enclosed absent. Risso/Clark Exmouth locality insufficient British evidence, actual Jeffreys dredging localities and depths distinguished from general belief about coasts. Numbered responses run1st,2nd,3rd,5; no fourth reconstructed. Advises selective distinct synonyms while deferring to Darwin, requests adopted labels. Later1854 classifications and publication not contemporary agreed answer or proof delivered copy.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1554A: February21,1854 complete four-page ALS. Seven blocks, fourteen footnotes and bibliography. Missing King October26 letter arrived about a week earlier, not exact February14; presumed prior year remains inference. Raw HTML repeats Beagle/booms/trade-wind clause within P1, with childred spelling; preserve textual defect as rendering hold rather than silently repair. Reminiscence, seven children/five sons, emigration worries and health are Darwin personal voice; Strzelecki identification and Macarthur kinship explicitly uncertain, Norman dinner and Covington reports distinct routes. Requests Scalpellum duplicate only if father has/finds one. Charles Stokes death differs from John Lort Stokes naval news; possible expedition appointment remains hearsay, later nonappointment separate. Imminent war wording retained independently of apparatus January1854 assertion; no later event backdated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1624: Incomplete two-page Knox ALS with missing opening. Three blocks, five footnotes, Darwin annotations and bibliography. Raw XML has three mutually exclusive March windows in1855,1856,1857, all approximate/questioned, not continuous March1855–March1857. Birds next-month plan and stomach-seed processing proposed, seeks refreshed directions. Pike transfer by cormorant feet/gullet is Knox childhood hypothesis prompted by Darwin hint, not witnessed transfer. Later uncertain-memory and cormorant remarks are expressly CD annotations, not Knox written annotation; missing subsequent letter and annotation date not reconstructed. Proof chapter edition uncertain and July1852 book reading separate from this date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1465: December21, supplied1851 ALS. Three blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Requests Conia rosea loan or minimum valves and whether personally collected; Australian form currently only closely allied, not yet proven identical. Promise of safe return is future. Later1854 naming, unique specimen acknowledgment and identity conclusion cannot be imported into1851 request. No Krauss reply body preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1472A: January30, supplied1852 complete ALS. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Twenty copies received by writing; erroneous bound material enclosed but not reproduced. Leighton volume origin only perhaps, removal requested not accomplished. Darwin personal surviving copy lacking material does not prove all twenty copies already corrected. Missing binder address does not authorize invented binder correspondence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1794: December9,1855 complete seven-page ALS. Eight blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Layard publications read, direct approach for information and long-bred Cape pigeon/duck/poultry skins contingent on available fanciers/time; old dying birds/bones specifications not collection completed. European breed loss/modification a hypothesis. Andersson account promised not received. P7–8 after closing are authorial continuation concerning Ceylon fanciers, proposed Thwaites approach and Benson uncertain shell locality. Benson memorandum1790P5–6 uniquely supports cross-correspondent use by December9; already known by December7 reply4354, so new witness does not move earliest known date later. Raw stemostoma here versus stenostoma in1790 preserved. Later books and December10 Thwaites approach remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1593: September19,1854 Lowe ALS. Nine blocks, six footnotes, Darwin annotation and bibliography. Distinguishes representative sets by regional facies with ambiguous individual exceptions; insufficient NW African data, not universal certainty. Extinction counts distinguish forms versus species: Madeira10/~35 forms,6–7/35species; PortoSanto7–8/~60forms,5–6/55–56species, approximations retained. New Helix fausta varieties b/c classification and not recently restudied PortoSanto material. Cirripedia disposal at Wollaston proposed and complete set saved, not explicit receipt. Greek word examples are raw cqalla/vaqacla/uqacla/rparla/arla with underline, no alternate encoded Greek; rendering held. Rabbits common European origin belief without close examination. Darwin facies-heredity annotation undated, not Lowe assertion or exact letter-date Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-372: Fresh earlier context: Wednesday assigned August9,1837 ALS. Four blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Missing Horner note cancels tomorrow invitation, Darwin proposes Monday unless contrary reply; Friday FitzRoy work plan, not witnessed attendance. Wedding cake arrived from Shrewsbury this morning and accompanying portion forwarded, no recipient arrival proved. Authorial request after main paragraph precedes signature; brotherly cake joke belongs to Charles voice, no current1851 antecedent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-648: Fresh earlier context: Tuesday assigned October4,1842 ALS. Three blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Thanks missing Horner congratulations, reports Emma improved postpartum and attributes recovery to country air as own belief. Down access/quiet and moving expense described, Erasmus joke later revised on visit. Received enthusiastic Lyell Coral-volume letter, Horner illness and hoped recovery. November Geological Society business prospective; actual December election not backdated. Lonsdale gift gratitude observed but source letters/gift documentation outside this body. No1842 postpartum prompt becomes1851 mourning inquiry.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1218: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Sunday circa February 1849. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1285: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Tuesday January 1850. Missing William Hooker account improves Darwin fears for Joseph safety and collection; does not prove he knew December 23 release or later annexation described in apparatus. Earlier geological letter forwarded by Henslow mentioned without identifying content; cannot uniquely map to 1257 or other Hooker letter on generic subject alone. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1331: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 22, supplied 1850. Forwards Joseph Hooker letter to William, then requests onward Henslow circulation. Specific geological motto and complimentary book discussion identify 1257 independently of generic Dear Darwin salutation; apparatus explicitly confirms September 30 letter. Darwin already read it by May 22, improving previously recorded June 13 witness from 1339. This is cross-correspondent knowledge/routing, not a direct answer to Joseph. record_notes.DCP-LETT-679: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1371: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November26Silchar: acknowledges letter debt and explains renewed Falconer withholding; routine for three months afterApril followed by six mails missing, while an English proof parcel actually arrived today without letter and was discarded. Retain exception to rhetorical sends nothing. Current/anticipated route via Manipurfrontier, Sylhet, Chittagong, Arracan/Ceylon and return is prospective. P7–14 specifically answers1339 transverse-river/double-chain argument, distinguishes watershed axis from line of highest snowy peaks using labeled diagram, tests definitions of geological/geographical chain and argues denudation/river organization; does not simply accept two parallel chains. P15 report of Darwin BritishAssociation presence concerns1849meeting via delayed news, not proof1850attendance. P16 records roots in underclay but failed search for McClelland fossil beach, distant views stated as estimates. P17 promises barnacles, contrasts tropical low-altitude oaks and high palms with fossil-climate assumptions, adds Tibetan camel/elephant reports; later journal says barnacles notcollected, so promise is not shipment. P18 classifies Khasi boulders as denudation rather than ice. Expects reunion before an answer, not proof no answer exists. One source diagram and separate undated Darwin pencil score read.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1790: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 5, 1855 signed Benson memorandum, main P1–14 fully read. reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
